newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - NZ Business weeklies - July 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - NZ Business weeklies - July 25.

text.p: THE NATIONAL BUSINESS REVIEW

Minister sued for $7 million over heart-unit row: The row over the Christchurch heart unit sent the coalition a step closer to cardiac arrest this week as Health Minister Bill English was hit with a $7.7 million damages claim. Page 1.
Britomart float beckons: The $135 million float of Britomart developer Pacific Capital Assets also could be just the start of another infrastructure projects in Australia and Asia. Page 1.
CEOs unimpressed with Bolger's performance: Prime Minister Jim Bolger's approval rating from business leaders has plummeted in the last three months. Page 1.

IRD blows whistle on sports workers: As it blows the whistle for a fair approach to sports-worker tax, Inland Revenue has admitted that intention in a sports contract is a key element in deciding whether a sportsman or woman is a self-employed contractor. Page 2.

Maori launch series of hui to debate future of $300 million fisheries assets: Maori are meeting in Wellington this weekend to consider how to share $300 million of fishing assets won through treaty negotiations. Page 4.

New chain springs up from ashes of Underground: Australian listed retailer Just Jeans admits it is recovering from a bad clothing year but hopes its expansion in New Zealand will boost profits. Page 5.

ECNZ counters Bradford criticism: ECNZ management and energy minister Max Bradford have clashed over whether a further breakup of the state-owned electricity generator would creat efficiencies. Page 10.
Ex-BellSouth chief takes Advantage: Former BellSouth chief executive Keith Davis has walked out of the corporate wilderness to lead another company -- Advantage Group. Page 10.
Real ATN crime was wasting $8 million: The pessimists said the pilot Maori television station in Auckland was set up to fail because the government was not giving it enough money to succeed. Page 11.

Public Trust privatisation urged in Business Roundtable report: Greater diversification into equities by government-guaranteed pension and savings fund will reduce contingent risks currently borne by taxpayers, a report prepared by CS Bost affiliate First NZ Capital says. Page 13.
THE INDEPENDENT BUSINESS WEEKLY

Another move to stymie winebox inquiry: A major stoush among winebox inquiry participants about the extent of document discovery is expected before Justice Robert Smellie at the High Court at Auckland this morning. Page 1.

Clark takes up cudgels for re-regulated taxi drivers: Labour leader Helen Clark is meeting Auckland International Airport bosses this morning to demand action in what's becoming a full scale war over taxi drivers' access to the airport. Page 3.

Project Hamburger: TVNZ trims the fat: Project Hamburger, the nickname given to the restructuring of TVNZ's television division, has taken the first six in what insiders are predicting will be a body count of 300, including long-standing executives. Page 3.

JB Were pioneers exchangeable notes: Exchangeable notes -- a new type of investment product best described as a cross between a term deposit and a share option -- will soon be available in New Zealand. Page 5.

Auckland developer targets Sydney buyers: New Zealand's tallest apartment building, The Metropolis, is being sold to Sydneysiders -- the first time a New Zealand residential project has been directly marketed in Australia. Page 6.

Sovereign aims to break the banks' mortgage stranglehold: Sovereign Assurance aims to put a big dent in banks' home mortgage business by undercutting their mortgage rates by 0.25 percent to 0.5 percent and offering customers a wider range of borrowing options. Page 7.

Kiwi Income Property Trust managers ask for more: Managers of the listed Kiwi Income Trust are asking to be guaranteed compensation equivalent to one year's fees should they be removed from office. Page 7.
Powerco wins first round: Powerco this week won the first round in its fight for a substantial North Island base when the Commerce Commission okayed its bid to acquire Egmont Electricity. Page 7.
